title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.104-106 of Grothendieck's own numbering). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs' of a 1-dimensional tame object, modelled on an ordered line. The objects in M are points P_a and open segments S_ab (a<b). Finite unions of these are 'polygonales'. Each object has a boundary δ with an origin 'or' and an extremity 'ex'. The relations used are:
- Z |∘| Z': roughly, disjoint interiors.
- Z || Z': disjoint.
- <pos: lies strictly to the left.
From |∘| one gets a Galois-type polarity:
- cosupp°(Φ) = {Z' : Z' |∘| Y for all Y in Φ};
- supp°(Φ) = {Z : Z |∘| Z' for all Z' in cosupp°(Φ)}, a double-orthogonal closure.

Lemma (stated p.104). If Φ <pos X <pos Ψ, then supp°(Φ∪Ψ) = supp°(Φ) ∪ supp°(Ψ). In words, the closure is additive on two pieces separated by a point or segment X. The inclusion ⊃ is trivial. For ⊂, p.104 notes that X ∈ cosupp°(Φ∪Ψ). Hence any Z in supp°(Φ∪Ψ) satisfies Z |∘| X, so Z ≤pos X or Z ≥pos X.

This page proves: Z < X ⇒ Z ∈ supp°(Φ), and symmetrically Z > X ⇒ Z ∈ supp°(Ψ).

Proof of the first implication:
1. Take Z' ∈ cosupp°(Φ). We must show Z |∘| Z'. Since Z ∈ supp°(Φ∪Ψ), it suffices to show Z' |∘| Φ∪Ψ, i.e. that Z' |∘| Ψ as well.
2. Without loss of generality X is the canonical separator. Put a = ex δΦ and b = or δΨ; then X = P_a if a = b, and X = S_ab if a < b.
3. Since P_a is a boundary point of Φ and Z' |∘| Φ, we get Z' |∘| P_a or Z' = P_a. This is the 'trivial lemma' in the margin.
4. Case Z' = P_a. Then P_a |∘| Φ, and P_a |∘| Ψ because X <pos Ψ. So Z' |∘| Φ∪Ψ.
5. Otherwise Z' lies strictly on one side of a.
6. Case Z' <pos P_a. Then Z' <pos Ψ, so Z' || Ψ, and again Z' |∘| Φ∪Ψ.
7. Case P_a <pos Z' (finished on p.106). Here Z < X forces Z ≤ P_a, so Z <pos Z' and therefore Z |∘| Z'.

Grothendieck remarks on p.106 that the general hypothesis 'Hyp.' was not needed. The lemma feeds an induction on the number of connected components, part (v) of a structure statement on supp° of polygonals. It is followed by the 'composition of segments' lemma: supp°{S_ab, P_b, S_bc} = supp°(S_ac).
errors: Slip: 'P_a ∈ Z' |∘| Φ' should read 'P_a |∘| Φ' (P_a, being a boundary point of Φ, is interior-disjoint from Φ).
Step 5 (Z' ≠ P_a and Z' |∘| P_a ⇒ Z' lies entirely on one side of a) silently uses that elements of M are connected (points or segments); it is not valid for arbitrary parts.

In the case Z' >pos P_a, the argument does not establish Z' |∘| Ψ. It switches to proving Z |∘| Z' directly via Z ≤ P_a. This is legitimate, but the announced reduction 'il suffit que Z' |∘| Φ∪Ψ' is abandoned in that case.
The wording is muddled ('Z |∘| Ψ [?] – il suffit ...'). The intended reduction is clearly to show Z' |∘| Φ∪Ψ.

ideas.what: Closure supp° defined as double orthogonal with respect to an interior-disjointness relation |∘|, with cosupp° as the orthogonal
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / polarity closure; regular-open (double pseudocomplement) closure in mereotopology / contact algebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); Tarski and de Vries for point-free regular-region algebras
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Analysis situs notes (1986); the tame topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme

ideas.what: Additivity of the closure for two configurations separated by a point or segment (Φ <pos X <pos Ψ)
ideas.modern_name: Separation/additivity lemma for regular closure of 1-dimensional polyhedra

ideas.what: Canonical separator X = P_a or S_ab built from ex δΦ and or δΨ
ideas.modern_name: elementary order-theoretic construction on a linearly ordered 1-dimensional model

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatic analysis situs reconstructs topology from a disjointness/incidence relation via a double-orthogonal closure (supp°, cosupp°). This is essentially the point-free / mereotopological approach (contact algebras, Region Connection Calculus) and orthogonality spaces, which developed independently. The link between his tame-topology programme and region-based topology does not seem to be made in the literature. The content of this page itself is routine.
missed.quote: Soit donc Z' ∈ cosupp°(Φ), i.e. Z' |∘| Φ, nous devons prouver Z |∘| Z'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could situate Grothendieck's 'géométrie modérée' axiomatics within existing point-free topology and o-minimal combinatorics, but only marginally.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, correct case analysis inside a combinatorial lemma about 1-dimensional configurations. Its only interest is as part of the unpublished axiomatic tame-topology project.
transcription_corrections: 's-pr°(Φ)', 's-pr°(Ψ)', 's-pr°(Φ∪Ψ)' should read supp°(Φ), supp°(Ψ), supp°(Φ∪Ψ), consistent with the previous page.
'Cas où : "quelconque" X, OPS' likely reads '... OPS' = 'on peut supposer' X canonical.
'(on sait déjà ...)' likely '(on sait déjà Z < X et Z ∈ supp°(Φ∪Ψ))'.
Margin lemma: 'P_a Δ Y' is likely 'P_a ∈ δY' (P_a a boundary point of Y).
Second margin lemma: likely 'X <pos Ψ ⇒ X || Ψ' or similar (P_a |∘| Ψ), marked 'trivial'.
'105' at top is Grothendieck's own page number; '114' is the archive foliation.
